user.title: Add a Mysa thermostat
user.description:
Mysa Local controls Mysa thermostats over your own network (HomeKit), with Mysa's cloud as an optional extra.

Tested so far on the Mysa Baseboard Lite (BB-V2-0-L). Other models are supported through Mysa's capability data but are untested.

wifi_help.title: Put the thermostat on Wi-Fi
wifi_help.description:
A new or reset Mysa shows a Bluetooth icon. Put it on your 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi with the browser-based setup page: [{url}]({url}). It works in Chrome or Edge on a computer with Bluetooth and doesn't need the Mysa app or a phone.

Once it's on Wi-Fi, Home Assistant discovers it. Submit to go back.

pick.title: Pick a thermostat
pick.description: Unpaired Mysa thermostats found on your network. If yours isn't listed, press a button on it (an unpaired Mysa's HomeKit service dozes off), check it's on Wi-Fi ([setup page]({url})) and that it isn't paired to Apple Home or another controller.

pair.title: Pair {name}

takeover_confirm.title: Move {name} to Mysa Local
takeover_confirm.description: Mysa Local adds its own HomeKit pairing to {name} through the existing one, so you don't need the setup code. Its entities keep their entity IDs, names and area, and the HomeKit Device entry is removed afterwards. {error}

cloud_offer.title: Mysa cloud (optional)
cloud_offer.description: Signing in to Mysa is optional. Everything local already works; the next step lists what signing in adds.

cloud_login.title: Sign in to Mysa [optional]
cloud_login.description:
Signing in to Mysa is optional: everything local works without it. It adds:
- Button lock, display brightness, setpoint limits, temperature offset and heater type
- Mysa schedules and holds
- Firmware update checks
- The thermostat's own measured heating runtime
- Control through Mysa's cloud while the local connection is down

Your password is stored only if you tick **Save my password**. Otherwise Home Assistant keeps just a sign-in token.

data_description.save_password: Stored unencrypted in Home Assistant's configuration, as most integrations store theirs. Mysa Local then signs in again by itself when the Mysa sign-in expires (it seems to last about a month). Without it, Home Assistant asks you to sign in again. To change this later, sign out and sign in again.

cloud_devices.title: Thermostats from your account
cloud_devices.description: Pick the thermostats to add. For each one with HomeKit, you're then offered to pair it locally too, so it keeps working without Mysa's servers; skip that and it's controlled through Mysa's cloud.

finish.title: Untested model
finish.description: The {model} hasn't been tested with Mysa Local yet. It should work through Mysa's capability data, but some features may be missing or wrong. After setup, please download the diagnostics and share them in an issue on GitHub, so it can be marked as tested.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in to Mysa again
reauth_confirm.description: The stored Mysa sign-in stopped working. Local control keeps working in the meantime. If you saved your password at sign-in, the one you enter here replaces it.

account.title: Add {name} to your Mysa account?
account.description: {name} isn't on your Mysa account. Adding it lets Home Assistant use the Mysa cloud for it: button lock, brightness, setpoint limits, schedules, firmware checks and control through the cloud while the local connection is down. Local control works either way. {error}

data.add_to_account: Add it to my Mysa account

local_offer.title: Pair {name} locally too?
local_offer.description: {name} is controlled through Mysa's cloud. Paired over HomeKit as well, Home Assistant controls it on your own network and keeps working when Mysa's servers or your internet are down. You need the 8-digit HomeKit code from the back of the faceplate.

local_not_found.title: {name} wasn't found on your network
local_not_found.description:
Home Assistant looked for {name}'s HomeKit service (it advertises as {homekit_name}) and didn't find it.

- Press a button on the thermostat: an unpaired Mysa's HomeKit service dozes off until then. Wait a few seconds and try again.
- If it's paired to Apple Home or another HomeKit controller, remove it there first.
- If it isn't on Wi-Fi, use the [setup page]({url}).

abort.already_configured: This thermostat is already set up.

abort.no_homekit_device_entries: No Mysa thermostats were found in the HomeKit Device integration.
abort.wrong_account: That's a different Mysa account from the one set up.
abort.wrong_thermostat: That was a different thermostat, not {name}, so its new pairing was removed again.

account_remove.title: Remove {name} from your Mysa account?
account_remove.description:
Home Assistant takes {name} out of your Mysa account's Home/Away/Vacation shortcuts, deletes its Mysa schedule, then removes it from the account. The Mysa app won't show it anymore. Mysa keeps its settings, so adding it back later restores them.

It stays in Home Assistant ({local}). Without the account its cloud extras stop working, and a thermostat that's only connected through the cloud can't be reached at all. {error}

name_from_mysa.title: Rename {name} to {cloud_name}?
name_from_mysa.description: The thermostat is called **{name}** in Home Assistant and **{cloud_name}** in the Mysa app. This renames it in Home Assistant to **{cloud_name}**. Its entity names follow (unless you've renamed them yourself); entity IDs stay the same.

name_to_mysa.title: Rename {cloud_name} in the Mysa app?
name_to_mysa.description: The thermostat is called **{cloud_name}** in the Mysa app. This renames it there to **{name}**, its Home Assistant name. {error}

data_description.cloud_enabled: Off: no calls to Mysa's servers at all, and the cloud-only entities are disabled (they keep their names and history, and come back when you turn the cloud on). Your sign-in is kept, so turning it back on needs no password.
data_description.scan_interval: How often to read all thermostats from the cloud (one request per poll). Local HomeKit updates are instant regardless.
data_description.live_mode: While a thermostat can't be reached on your network, ask Mysa to have it report every ~5 s, and read the cloud every 10 s. Never used while the local connection works. Off: the cloud is read at the interval above, and its readings are often 15–30 minutes old.

data_description.allow_firmware_install: Lets the Firmware entity install updates Mysa offers. Untested, and an install can't be undone.

local_unreachable.title: {name} isn't reachable on your network
local_unreachable.description:
Home Assistant hasn't reached {name} over HomeKit (last address {host}) for {minutes} minutes, and the Mysa cloud isn't available as a fallback.

Check that the thermostat has power and is on Wi-Fi, and give it a DHCP reservation on your router so its address doesn't change. This message clears itself once the thermostat is back.

local_unreachable_cloud.title: {name} is running on the Mysa cloud
local_unreachable_cloud.description:
Home Assistant hasn't reached {name} over HomeKit (last address {host}) for {minutes} minutes, so it's being controlled through Mysa's cloud for now.

Check that the thermostat is on the same network as Home Assistant, and give it a DHCP reservation on your router so its address doesn't change. This message clears itself once the local connection is back.

hold.name: Hold
hold.description: Holds a setpoint over the thermostat's Mysa schedule, permanently or until a time. Needs a Mysa schedule on the thermostat.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.description: Setpoint to hold. Defaults to the current setpoint.

hvac_mode.name: Mode
hvac_mode.description: Mode to hold. Defaults to the current mode.

until.name: Until
until.description: End of the hold. Leave empty for a permanent hold.

resume_schedule.name: Resume schedule
resume_schedule.description: Ends a hold, so the thermostat follows its Mysa schedule again.

set_schedule.name: Set schedule
set_schedule.description: Replaces the weekly schedule stored on Mysa's side. It keeps running even when Home Assistant or the internet is down.

events.name: Events
events.description: List of events, each with days (mon to sun), time (HH:MM), temperature and optionally hvac_mode.
